venture.summary: Each of the seven co-founders plans to sell exactly the same number of shares in the IPO, which would bring each of them about $250 million in cash at the midpoint of the price range while leaving the group in control of the company.

venture.summary: OpenAI has not yet said what its plans are for the future of travel. But Sonder founder Francis Davidson is a well-known figure in the travel industry.

research.headline: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions
research.summary: Foundation models trained on large unlabeled corpora develop emergent capabilities, tasks that go beyond the training objective. We extend this paradigm to multimodal biology with Bonbon, a foundation model for molecular interactions trained on approximately 3.2 trillion tokens of paired protein-ligand sequences. From a single representation space, Bonbon exhibits three zero-shot emergent capabilities at hierarchical levels of resolution: functional (mechanism of action), residue (binding site localization, including orthosteric/allosteric discrimination), and bond (covalent versus non-covalent engagement).

research.headline: Toward Foundation Detection Models via Example-Based Grounding in EM-DETR
research.summary: DeepLearning (DL)-based Computer-Aided Diagnostic (CAD) systems have shown great promise in supporting clinicians, but their performance heavily depends on the availability of large, well-annotated datasets. In medical lesion detection, the scarcity of comprehensive, stan dardized annotations and the heterogeneity of existing datasets limit the development of robust foundation models. In this work, we introduce a novel approach to building a multi-domain foundation model for le sion detection by integrating diverse medical image datasets annotated for both anatomical structures and abnormalities.

research.headline: Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents
research.summary: Predicting how a ligand binds to its target is central to small-molecule drug discovery. Modern cofolding models can generate diverse candidate poses, but reliably ranking these candidates remains challenging. We introduce Pyrite, a pairwise pose-ranking benchmark comprising 1,500 pose pairs across diverse protein-ligand complexes.

research.headline: Innovating with AI in the special chemicals industry
research.summary: As companies look to accelerate innovation with artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and advanced modeling, the primary challenge is connecting new technologies to reliable data, scientific expertise, and the practical realities of bringing products to market. For specialty chemicals manufacturer Lubrizol, digital transformation is all about giving researchers the tools to test ideas faster, make better-informed….

research.headline: When Does the Real Wiring Win? Testing connectome structure-function claims against unmeasured physiology
research.summary: Connectome-constrained models are often used to argue that a measured wiring diagram outperforms shuffled or rewired wiring, and hence that structure shapes function. Such comparisons can confound wiring with how the models are tuned: a connectome fixes who connects to whom, not the excitability, gains or plasticity rates the model also needs, and modellers often tune these until the real-wiring model works. We separate three estimands: physiology tuned on the real wiring and transferred to nulls (P1), each wiring tuned on its own (P2), and P2 restricted to physiology consistent with independent data (P3).

Earlier this year, Claude Code went through its own particular hype cycle. And now, Anthropic is trying to expand its footprint […].

The Nvidia CEO runs one of the world's most valuable companies, controls the in-demand technology fueling the AI boom, and is cozy with presidents, CEOs, and all manner of important people. regulatory.headline: FTC Settles With Stream Auto Outlet Over Deceptive Pricing Allegations
regulatory.summary: The Federal Trade Commission announced an agreement with Stream Auto Outlet to resolve deceptive advertising claims. The Long Island, New York-based dealership group allegedly advertised vehicle prices far lower than what consumers ultimately had to pay.

regulatory.headline: Federal Court Halts Phantom Debt Scheme Following FTC Action
regulatory.summary: A federal court temporarily halted a debt collection operation and froze its assets at the Federal Trade Commission's request. The complaint alleges the operators used false threats to collect over $20 million in often-fictitious debts from consumers. Deceptive and unlawful tactics were allegedly used to pressure individuals into paying debts they frequently did not owe.

regulatory.headline: Progress Residential and Pretium Partners Pay $49.75 Million to Settle FTC Charges
regulatory.summary: Progress Residential and owner Pretium Partners agreed to pay $49.75 million to settle charges brought by the FTC and four states over deceptive rental pricing practices. The proposed order requires the companies to advertise true rental prices, disclose all fees clearly, and stop improperly withholding security deposits. The settlement resolves allegations that the nation's largest single-family rental property manager misled consumers.

regulatory.headline: Five States Join FTC Lawsuit Alleging Hims and Hers Engaged in Deceptive and Unlawful Privacy Practices
regulatory.summary: The Federal Trade Commission filed an amended complaint adding five states as co-plaintiffs in its lawsuit alleging that telehealth provider Hims and Hers shared consumers’ sensitive health information with third-party advertising platforms, despite claiming its services maintain consumers’ privacy, and it deceived users about its billing and cancellation practices.

regulatory.headline: New Details Emerge in Amazon Ads Auction-Rigging Case
regulatory.summary: Newly unredacted material sheds light on Amazon’s alleged scheme to manipulate auction results to meet corporate financial targets The Federal Trade Commission and 22 states recently filed an updated version of their complaint against Amazon with unredacted details about Amazon’s alleged use of deceptive and unfair practices to secretly inflate prices in its online search advertising auction.

frontier.headline: Nonperturbative string dynamics in a (2+1)D lattice gauge theory on a superconducting quantum processor
frontier.summary: Electric flux strings underpin confinement in gauge theories. In two spatial dimensions, their evolution involves competing processes of charge motion, pair creation, and transverse deformation. Accessing these dynamics beyond perturbative limits challenges classical approaches, as entanglement growth restricts the times accessible to tensor-network simulations.

frontier.headline: The energetic cost of loading classical data in quantum computers
frontier.summary: Quantum algorithms for machine learning, chemistry, and cryptanalysis often assume coherent access to classical data at negligible physical cost. We instead treat data loading as a hardware process and quantify the dynamic energetic cost of a quantum random access memory (QRAM) query on a superconducting processor. Using the metric-noise-resource framework, we relate query fidelity and power to gate duration, relative two-qubit drive strength, and the distribution of attenuation across a multi-stage refrigerator, while accounting for thermal photons and gate errors.

frontier.headline: Implementing rapid reset of superconducting qubits with on-chip dissipation
frontier.summary: Rapid and high-fidelity qubit reset is essential for quantum state initialization and quantum error correction. Conventional reset protocols for superconducting qubits often rely on dissipative elements connected to external circuitry, exposing qubits to thermal noise from higher-temperature environments. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a scalable approach to qubit reset and leakage removal over multiple transmon qubits using dedicated dissipation units comprising resonators coupled to on-chip resistive loads.

frontier.headline: Alzheimer’s may have early warning signs outside the brain
frontier.summary: A surprising discovery suggests that some early signs of Alzheimer’s disease may begin outside the brain. Using miniature laboratory systems made from human cells, scientists found that genetic mutations associated with inherited Alzheimer’s can disrupt nerve-to-muscle connections without any involvement from the brain or spinal cord. This could help explain why some patients experience changes in balance, walking, and coordination long before memory problems develop.

industry.summary: Creators in their sixties, seventies, and eighties have flooded adult platforms as the demand for mature content has skyrocketed, with some turning to online sex work as a retirement lifeline.

industry.summary: A day after the US midterm elections gave Democrats control of Congress, Onion CEO Ben Collins and comedian Patti Harrison spoke to WIRED about the salve of satire during politically fraught times.

voices.headline: The Inconvenient Truth at the Center of the Immigration Debate
voices.summary: Have liberals learned anything from the border crisis that helped return Donald Trump to office two years ago? Many have not, if a recent report from the American Civil Liberties Union is any indication. The group claims to offer a “way forward” for the country’s asylum system, which has become a back door for economic migrants.

voices.headline: The Lost World of Aquaterra
voices.summary: Illustrations by Owen Pomery Imagine a planet that’s home not only to the seven continents you know but also to an immense feature you’ve never heard of, continental in scale. Extending along the world’s coastal shelves from the tropics almost to the poles, this place is roughly equivalent in size to South America, with a total area of more than 6.6 million square miles. During the last Ice Age, it consisted almost entirely of lowland ecosystems: cold grasslands and tundras in the far north, grazed by woolly mammoths and steppe bison; temperate woodlands and open country in the middle latitudes, home to aurochs, horses, and giant elk; tropical forests, grasslands, and mangrove swamps near the equator, inhabited by Stegodons, Asian hippos, and Komodo dragons; and dry scrub in the far south, roamed by marsupial lions, giant flightless birds, and lizards the size of crocodiles.

voices.headline: The Left’s Election Denial
voices.summary: B ernie Sanders and his acolytes have spent the past decade insisting that Democrats would command national majorities if only they embraced his left-wing policies. After last week’s election, the movement claimed vindication. The results proved that “we can win over millions of Republicans and independents who are struggling economically if we focus on the issues that are important,” Sanders told Politico .

voices.headline: Getting Too Close to Trump Was a Mistake
voices.summary: O ver the past week , following MAGA’s significant losses in the midterms, I have been asked the same questions again and again: How could Silicon Valley have gotten it so wrong? Why did tech leaders not anticipate the consequences of joining themselves at the hip to MAGA straight after Donald Trump won reelection in 2024? What follows is not a critique of the individual tech leaders themselves—some were more restrained than others—nor is it a personal commentary on Mark Zuckerberg, my former boss.

voices.headline: Pete Hegseth Lashes Out
voices.summary: Pete Hegseth was in my neighborhood today. I live just up the road from the Naval War College, where I taught for 25 years, and where Hegseth gave a speech this morning about the future of military education. But “speech” may be too generous.
